facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Overall, Chord presents medium governance risk. The supported behaviour is large, cash-flow-funded shareholder returns with a falling share count, which matters because distributions near free cash flow leave little room to absorb a price fall or a debt-funded deal, and implies that creditor protection rests on leverage staying low rather than on structural restraint. Countervailing evidence is a base-only dividend, a declining payout share in 2026 and no documented creditor-adverse action. facts.text: The strongest evidence for a benign reading is that no sponsor exists, no liability-management or priming action is documented, the 2025 refinancing replaced notes with longer unsecured notes, and 2026 returns used under half of free cash flow with no new debt. The view would turn adverse if the Marcellus Shale proceeds or a new borrowing funded distributions above free cash flow, if a debt-funded acquisition followed the XTO deal, or if the unsupplied credit agreement shows wide capacity for restricted payments after the amendments. It would improve if a compliance certificate and the agreements show tight restricted-payment limits, or if the explanation of the chief executive change shows continuity of the capital-return policy. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Chord's transactions follow a consistent pattern of buying scale with stock, cash and notes and then pruning. The Enerplus combination in May 2024 paid USD 375.8 million in cash and issued shares, and the XTO assets bought in October 2025 cost USD 540.4 million, funded by the 2030 notes and cash. The company issued two series of senior unsecured notes in 2025, USD 750.0 million due 2033 in March and USD 750.0 million due 2030 in September, using the first to repurchase and discharge the 2026 notes and the second to fund the XTO purchase. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a strong reading is that FY2025 net profit was close to nil after the impairment with gross leverage of 0.89x, and that the 2026 recovery came with an oil price that management links to the Middle East conflict and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The view would weaken if the crude sales price fell back to the FY2025 level while buybacks continued, if the Marcellus Shale proceeds or new borrowing funded distributions above free cash flow, or if the unsupplied covenant terms are tighter than the headline liquidity implies. It would strengthen if hedge cover for 2027 rose well above a quarter of volumes at floors near USD 65.54 per Bbl, if buybacks were kept below free cash flow, or if a compliance certificate showed wide headroom. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Chord is an independent oil and gas producer whose cash flow comes from crude oil sold to refiners and marketers from the Williston Basin, with a limited non-operated gas interest in the Marcellus Shale that is held for sale. It operates most of its portfolio, markets its own production, and has been built through the Whiting merger of 2022, the Enerplus combination of 2024 and the XTO purchase of 2025; the single basin and single product give cash-flow visibility only to the extent hedges and the oil price allow. facts.text: Revenue is price-driven and not contractually recurring. Production revenue rose with the crude sales price from USD 64.73 to USD 83.54 per Bbl between nine months 2025 and nine months 2026, while the quarterly price fell 8.71% from the second to the third quarter of 2026, which shows the volatility that creditors carry. Chord is a price taker; its levers are volume and marketing, and purchased oil and gas sales add revenue at close to nil margin. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Rivalry and substitutes matter through price: Chord is a price taker in a commodity market, and energy-transition and supply decisions by other producers set the price that drives cash flow. Buyer power is concentrated but limited on price because realised prices follow NYMEX WTI and other purchasers exist, while supplier power shows in service-cost inflation and in a limited set of midstream providers; new entrants are unlikely to match the acreage position quickly, an Analyst Judgement that supports Chord's standing without changing price exposure. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the near-term outlook is supportive but price-contingent. Tailwinds are the higher oil price, improved Williston Basin takeaway, a hedge floor on 47.27% of fourth-quarter 2026 volumes and the Marcellus Shale proceeds; headwinds are cost inflation, a rate rise in the third quarter of 2026 that tightens financial conditions, geopolitical reversal and the open 2027 hedge book. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside is a return of the crude price to the FY2025 average of USD 62.78 per Bbl, 18.61% below the last-twelve-months average of USD 77.13 per Bbl, while distributions continue. On last-twelve-months volumes that price would cut revenue and EBITDA by the same amount, leaving EBITDA at 72.74% of its reported level and net leverage at 0.30x, or 0.34x after the buybacks to 2026-11-04; free cash flow would fall to 79.08% of distributions, so distributions would run at 1.26x free cash flow, although the annualised base dividend alone would still be covered. The break comes in cash, not in debt service: cash would cover 5.35 years of that shortfall, buybacks of USD 529.0 million capacity could be stopped, capital spending could be cut, and no maturity falls due before 2030. This is an Analyst Judgement anchored to the reported FY2025 price; it omits hedge settlements and lower production taxes, so it overstates the near-term shortfall. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Chord presents a strong liquidity and refinancing position and an adequate business profile, supported by low reported leverage, USD 2,774.4 million of liquidity and operator control, but credit quality is constrained by price dependence, a payout policy that has run near free cash flow and an unsupplied legal framework. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: strong at the current price and contingent on hedges and spending cuts if prices fall. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the oil price and on whether distributions stay below free cash flow, since nothing matures before 2030. The primary downside path is a crude price fall that turns free cash flow below distributions and draws down cash. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, covenant figures, an agency view and 2027 guidance. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation P1; calculation P8

spans.text: ## Request

Chord Energy Corp (chrd-1486159), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway: Financial foundation built from the two annual reports and three quarterly reports supplied, through the quarter ended 2026-09-30. It states reported figures and labelled calculations only and draws no investment recommendation.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_chrd_chrd-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2024 | 2025-02-27 | 8396d4975918ffe796d5bf0565fe8b45cb5fbd173b0dfb63c0a4ab608ef08297 | FY2024 statements and the 2024 debt, used where a later report restates nothing |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_chrd_chrd-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-05-07 | 70dba078fdcc2ed69f65b9319073518f5e4e81363db7d0aa5403016a306a8a27 | Cash and undrawn capacity at 2026-03-31 |

| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness | CP-0 | 5202d82572c76c586561cf1067a1c7db58a13a1c2dd5c48deb6b6d51727e0455 | Source limitations, period map and the absence of legal documents, ratings and market data |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Chord's reported balance sheet is lightly levered and the fall in leverage over 2026 is real, so creditors hold thick earnings cover over debt that matures no earlier than 2030. Net debt was 0.22x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 0.77x at FY2025 and 0.36x at FY2024, with USD 2,774.4 million of liquidity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–127; calculation C1; calculation C2

The comfort rests on derived EBITDA at oil prices well above 2025 levels, and on cash that includes a refundable sale deposit. EBITDA is derived because the issuer states none, interim cash interest is not printed, and covenant ratios are not reported, so headroom is not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Analysis

Leverage is low and the improvement is not an artefact of the 2025 impairment. Excluding that non-cash charge, net debt over EBITDA was 0.58x at FY2025, still more than twice the 0.22x at 2026-09-30. Gross debt is almost unchanged since FY2025 while cash rose, so the fall comes from cash build and a larger EBITDA base, not from repayment.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 126–127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; calculation C3; calculation C4

Interest cover is very high, though the FY2025 cash-basis figure of 32.26x understates the cost of the 2025 notes, which were outstanding for only part of that year. On last-twelve-months EBITDA the full coupons on the two notes are covered 32.27x and interest expense is covered 28.88x.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C5; calculation C6

Cash flow converts well and funds shareholder returns without new debt. Free cash flow of USD 1,307.73 million in nine months 2026 was about half of EBITDA, and buybacks plus dividends took 48.77% of it, so the remainder built cash. Working capital was neutral: receivables rose while payables rose by a similar amount.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C7; calculation C8

Liquidity is ample and maturity risk is distant. Undrawn commitments of USD 1,969.7 million sit on top of cash, no debt falls due before the 2030 notes, and the October 2026 amendment moved the revolver maturity to 2031, with a springing maturity ahead of the 2030 notes only if more than USD 100.0 million remains and utilisation exceeds 80%.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation C1

Definitions change the headline in three places. Cash includes a refundable USD 55.0 million deposit for the Marcellus Shale sale, which would lift net leverage to 0.24x if excluded. Derivative settlements sit in investing activities and are outside the derived EBITDA, so cash earnings after hedge payments were lower than EBITDA suggests. Carrying-value debt is USD 17.755 million below principal because of unamortised financing costs.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; calculation C9; calculation C10

A non-debt funding float is growing: royalties payable and revenue suspense rose 30.84% from FY2025 to 2026-09-30. It costs no interest but is owed to royalty owners and partners and tracks revenue, so it would unwind if revenue fell.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C16

Data quality limits three conclusions. Nine-month 2026 net income includes an out-of-period tax benefit of USD 41.8 million that does not touch EBITDA; the issuer prints no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or covenant ratio; and interim cash interest paid is not printed, so cover on a cash basis is available only for full years.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; Source readiness (CP-0)

After the balance-sheet date, share repurchases of USD 91.0 million through 2026-11-04 would lift net debt to pro forma levels with net leverage of 0.25x. The pending sale of the Marcellus Shale interest, with estimated gross proceeds of USD 550.0 million, cannot be reflected because closing, net proceeds and the EBITDA sold are not stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

spans.text: ## Request

Chord Energy Corp (chrd-1486159), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway: Business & governance from the two annual reports and three quarterly reports supplied, through the quarter ended 2026-09-30. It covers the business, ownership and control, operating model, issuer history and governance behaviour, and draws no ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery view.
## Sources

| 10-K_2024-12-31_chrd_chrd-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2024 | 2025-02-27 | 8396d4975918ffe796d5bf0565fe8b45cb5fbd173b0dfb63c0a4ab608ef08297 | History of the combinations, the 2024 acquisition terms, dividends of 2024 |

| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness | CP-0 | 5202d82572c76c586561cf1067a1c7db58a13a1c2dd5c48deb6b6d51727e0455 | Source set, limitations and the absence of legal documents, ratings and market data |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Chord is a scaled, single-basin oil producer with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so creditors face concentration and capital-return risk, not extraction risk, and governance risk is medium. Distributions took 106.10% of free cash flow in FY2024 and 98.54% in FY2025, then 48.77% in nine months 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

The pattern that matters is debt-funded acquisition followed by a cash build as higher oil prices lifted cash flow: net debt rose USD 484.4 million during 2025 and the Marcellus Shale sale for USD 550.0 million is pending. The credit agreement is unsupplied and the signing chief executive changed without explanation, so capacity and continuity are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-06-30_chrd_chrd-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C7; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

The business is large and concentrated, which gives creditors scale but little diversification. Chord operates almost entirely in one basin with one reportable segment, crude oil is 91.73% of oil, NGL and gas revenues and 56% of proved reserves, and the company operates 89% of its reserves on acreage that is almost all held by production, so it can pace capital spending.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation C1

Customer and takeaway concentration are the operating dependencies that matter most to cash flow. Phillips 66 took 21% and Marathon Petroleum Supply & Trading 12% of FY2025 product sales, and the annual report names a limited number of midstream providers and a possible Dakota Access Pipeline shutdown as risks; an outage would force shut-ins or wider price differentials and cut cash flow, although management says other purchasers exist.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, and no extraction behaviour is documented, but shareholder returns are policy-driven and were large against free cash flow. The board is 82% independent, the variable dividend was dropped after 2024, and the share count fell 10.81% between February 2025 and October 2026, yet returns equalled 98.54% of FY2025 free cash flow, leaving no deleveraging cushion in a year of debt-funded acquisition.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 173; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2024-12-31_chrd_chrd-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

Growth has come through acquisitions funded partly with debt, so leverage rose in 2025 before falling in 2026. The Enerplus combination paid USD 375.8 million in cash and issued shares, and the XTO assets cost USD 540.4 million, funded from the 2030 notes and cash; the pending Marcellus Shale sale of USD 550.0 million points the other way, towards pruning a non-core interest.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_chrd_chrd-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C7; calculation C8

Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but thin on the points creditors rely on. The financial statements are audited and the quarterly reports are regular, but covenant compliance is stated without figures, the credit agreement was amended twice to raise baskets and thresholds without terms being supplied, and an 8.5% stake in a private specialty chemicals company with a Chord board designee is a related-party arrangement whose amounts are not stated.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; Source readiness (CP-0)

Overall, Chord presents medium governance risk. The supported behaviour is large, cash-flow-funded shareholder returns with a falling share count, which matters because distributions near free cash flow leave little room to absorb a price fall or a debt-funded deal, and implies that creditor protection rests on leverage staying low rather than on structural restraint. Countervailing evidence is a base-only dividend, a declining payout share in 2026 and no documented creditor-adverse action.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 173; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a benign reading is that no sponsor exists, no liability-management or priming action is documented, the 2025 refinancing replaced notes with longer unsecured notes, and 2026 returns used under half of free cash flow with no new debt. The view would turn adverse if the Marcellus Shale proceeds or a new borrowing funded distributions above free cash flow, if a debt-funded acquisition followed the XTO deal, or if the unsupplied credit agreement shows wide capacity for restricted payments after the amendments. It would improve if a compliance certificate and the agreements show tight restricted-payment limits, or if the explanation of the chief executive change shows continuity of the capital-return policy.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation C6
### Limitations
- Ownership and control are limited to no controlling holder identified, because the proxy statement is not supplied and holders above 5% and director holdings are not established.
- The signing chief executive differs between the second and third quarterly reports with no explanation, so continuity of the capital-return policy is assumed rather than shown.

- The 75% return tier of the policy cannot be tested because adjusted free cash flow and the forward EBITDA basis are not printed, so the pace of future distributions is a range rather than a forecast.
- Legal capacity for restricted payments, investments and liens cannot be assessed without the credit agreement and indentures, so the governance level reflects behaviour only.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Chord's transactions follow a consistent pattern of buying scale with stock, cash and notes and then pruning. The Enerplus combination in May 2024 paid USD 375.8 million in cash and issued shares, and the XTO assets bought in October 2025 cost USD 540.4 million, funded by the 2030 notes and cash. The company issued two series of senior unsecured notes in 2025, USD 750.0 million due 2033 in March and USD 750.0 million due 2030 in September, using the first to repurchase and discharge the 2026 notes and the second to fund the XTO purchase.

spans.text: ## Request

Chord Energy Corp (chrd-1486159), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway: Fundamental credit synthesis of business quality, financial profile, outlook and downside from the five filings and the three earlier analyses. It assigns no rating, draws no legal-capacity conclusion and sizes no position.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_chrd_chrd-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2024 | 2025-02-27 | 8396d4975918ffe796d5bf0565fe8b45cb5fbd173b0dfb63c0a4ab608ef08297 | History of the combinations and the 2024 distributions |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025 | 2026-02-26 | dc355741b318bdc39ae18eb221d1b766d464afdfd77ba79fc40846e063c49c09 | Business, reserves, customers, 2026 plan, covenant terms, return-of-capital policy, market-risk factors |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_chrd_chrd-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-05-07 | 70dba078fdcc2ed69f65b9319073518f5e4e81363db7d0aa5403016a306a8a27 | Period series only |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_chrd_chrd-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 | 2026-08-06 | 9b358b8c21b5b4d56ed1074092daf4f10131f5fc96a707947122b014a84c252a | Period series only |

| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness | CP-0 | 5202d82572c76c586561cf1067a1c7db58a13a1c2dd5c48deb6b6d51727e0455 | Source set and limitations |
| Financial foundation | CP-1 | 0e84607a711d20cbe00863e6c70c44556de4be0d334e5b6935be8b3cbfc9566d | Statements, leverage, cover, liquidity, maturities, pro forma net debt |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Chord's fundamentals are strong on liquidity, maturities and reported leverage but depend on an oil price well above 2025's, so a price fall would reach creditors through cash and distributions long before it threatened debt service.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Net debt was 0.22x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30, or 0.25x after USD 91.0 million of buybacks to 2026-11-04, with USD 2,774.4 million of liquidity and no maturity before the 2030 notes. At the FY2025 average crude price, 18.61% below the last-twelve-months average of USD 77.13 per Bbl, net leverage would be 0.30x and distributions 1.26x free cash flow, a gap that cash would cover for 5.35 years.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation P2; calculation P3; calculation P5; calculation P6; calculation P8
### Key findings

Liquidity and maturities are the strongest support. Liquidity of USD 2,774.4 million combines cash with USD 1,969.7 million of undrawn revolver commitments, the two notes of USD 750.0 million each fall due in 2030 and 2033 at fixed rates, and the revolver now matures in 2031; with nothing due for almost four years, refinancing risk is low and the revolver is a second line behind cash.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; calculation K3

Reported leverage is low and the fall since FY2025 is real: net debt over EBITDA was 0.22x at 2026-09-30 against 0.77x at FY2025 and 0.36x at FY2024, and 0.58x at FY2025 even after adding back the non-cash impairment. After USD 91.0 million of buybacks to 2026-11-04 it is 0.25x; the pro forma effect of the Marcellus Shale sale is not established because closing and net proceeds are not stated. EBITDA is derived, not issuer-stated, and excludes hedge settlements.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K4

Cash generation is strong at today's prices and entirely price-dependent. Free cash flow was USD 1,307.73 million in nine months 2026, 49.82% of EBITDA, because the average crude sales price was USD 83.54 per Bbl against USD 64.73 a year earlier and USD 62.78 in FY2025. Hedges cover 47.27% of fourth-quarter 2026 crude volumes but only 24.63% of last-twelve-months volumes for 2027 (31.15% with contracts added after the quarter), so most of the price exposure is open.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation K6; calculation H1; calculation H2; calculation H3

Business quality is average to strong on scale and cost control and weak on diversification. Crude oil is 91.73% of production revenue from one basin, Phillips 66 and Marathon Petroleum Supply & Trading took 21% and 12% of FY2025 sales, and 89% of reserves are operated on acreage that is almost all held by production, which lets Chord pace spending; lease operating expense per Boe rose to USD 10.24 in nine months 2026 from USD 9.74, so unit costs are drifting up.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41

Financial policy is the main discretionary risk. Distributions equalled 106.10% of free cash flow in FY2024 and 98.54% in FY2025 before falling to 48.77% in nine months 2026, and net debt rose USD 484.4 million in 2025 as acquisitions were paid with notes and cash; with no sponsor to extract value, the exposure is a payout policy that tiers up as leverage falls, which would use the cash cushion that currently supports the credit.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K7; calculation K8

Covenant headroom and legal capacity cannot be assessed. The revolver carries a leverage test below 3.50x and a current ratio test of at least 1.0x, compliance is stated without figures, and the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so strong liquidity is a statement about cash and undrawn commitments, not about what lenders could restrict.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a strong reading is that FY2025 net profit was close to nil after the impairment with gross leverage of 0.89x, and that the 2026 recovery came with an oil price that management links to the Middle East conflict and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The view would weaken if the crude sales price fell back to the FY2025 level while buybacks continued, if the Marcellus Shale proceeds or new borrowing funded distributions above free cash flow, or if the unsupplied covenant terms are tighter than the headline liquidity implies. It would strengthen if hedge cover for 2027 rose well above a quarter of volumes at floors near USD 65.54 per Bbl, if buybacks were kept below free cash flow, or if a compliance certificate showed wide headroom.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 126–127; calculation K1; calculation K11; calculation H2
### Limitations

- The downside scenario applies one price anchor to last-twelve-months volumes and leaves out hedge settlements and lower production taxes, so it overstates the near-term shortfall and understates exposure beyond the hedge horizon.

- Covenant ratios and the definitions behind them are not printed, so the liquidity and refinancing conclusions treat lender tests as untested, and headroom could be thinner than liquidity alone suggests.
- No production, price or cost guidance after February 2026 is supplied, so the twelve to twenty-four month outlook rests on reported run-rates and hedges rather than on management's plan.
- No agency rating or dated market price is supplied, so the market-access conclusion relies on the 2025 note issuance and not on where the notes trade.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The first strength is liquidity: USD 2,774.4 million of cash and undrawn commitments sit against no debt maturity until 2030, so a downturn would have to last years to threaten debt service, and the amended revolver extends the second line to 2031.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47

The second strength is low reported leverage with high interest cover: net debt over EBITDA of 0.22x (0.25x after USD 91.0 million of buybacks to 2026-11-04) and EBITDA covering interest expense 28.88x leave a wide cushion before debt service is pressured, although the cover is built on derived EBITDA at a high oil price.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K1; calculation K5

The third strength is operator control: 89% of reserves are operated and the acreage is almost all held by production, so Chord can cut capital spending in a downturn instead of losing most leases, which protects free cash flow when prices fall, although the annual report warns that some undeveloped leases expire unless drilled.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19
The fourth strength is the hedge book: collars and swaps cover 47.27% of fourth-quarter 2026 crude volumes, which sets a floor under near-term cash flow while leaving upside above the ceilings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation H1

The fifth strength is refinancing capacity: the 2025 issue of USD 750.0 million of notes due 2033 replaced notes due 2026 with unsecured debt and the revolver was extended twice, so lender appetite and market access were shown in 2025.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57

The first weakness is price dependence and concentration: crude oil is 91.73% of production revenue from one basin, so EBITDA moves with the oil price almost one for one, and a fall of 18.61% in the crude price would cut last-twelve-months EBITDA by 27.26%.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation P2; calculation P3; calculation P4

The second weakness is payout policy: distributions equalled 98.54% of FY2025 free cash flow, so little cash was left for debt reduction in a year when net debt rose USD 484.4 million, and the policy tiers up as leverage falls.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K7; calculation K8

The third weakness is customer and takeaway concentration: two purchasers took 21% and 12% of FY2025 sales and the annual report names reliance on a limited number of midstream providers and a possible Dakota Access Pipeline shutdown, either of which would cut volumes or widen differentials.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178

The fourth weakness is the unsupplied legal framework: two amendments raised baskets and thresholds without terms being supplied, so the capacity for distributions, new debt and liens is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57

The fifth weakness is event risk: the company has grown through three combinations since 2022, a Marcellus Shale sale is pending, and the signing chief executive changed without explanation, so strategy and leverage could shift quickly.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58
### Company description

Chord is an independent oil and gas producer whose cash flow comes from crude oil sold to refiners and marketers from the Williston Basin, with a limited non-operated gas interest in the Marcellus Shale that is held for sale. It operates most of its portfolio, markets its own production, and has been built through the Whiting merger of 2022, the Enerplus combination of 2024 and the XTO purchase of 2025; the single basin and single product give cash-flow visibility only to the extent hedges and the oil price allow.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36
### Ownership and group structure

Chord is widely held, with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so the credit does not carry sponsor extraction risk but also has no committed support. The borrower under the revolver is a subsidiary and certain subsidiaries guarantee the revolver and both notes, but the guarantors are not named, so structural priority cannot be assessed here; the business and governance review rates governance risk as medium because distributions have run near free cash flow and the credit agreement is unsupplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 165
### Revenue durability and pricing power

Revenue is price-driven and not contractually recurring. Production revenue rose with the crude sales price from USD 64.73 to USD 83.54 per Bbl between nine months 2025 and nine months 2026, while the quarterly price fell 8.71% from the second to the third quarter of 2026, which shows the volatility that creditors carry. Chord is a price taker; its levers are volume and marketing, and purchased oil and gas sales add revenue at close to nil margin.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation D1
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins can be defended at current prices but the cost trend is adverse. Lease operating expense per Boe rose from USD 9.74 to USD 10.24 and the production tax rate from 7.4% to 8.1% of oil, NGL and gas revenues, so costs absorb a share of any price gain; EBITDA margin on total revenues was 45.96% on the last twelve months against 34.19% in FY2025, a swing that is mostly price.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation K9
### Capital intensity and cash-flow conversion

EBITDA converts to free cash flow at about half in nine months 2026 and at 41.54% in FY2025, so capital spending absorbs roughly half of EBITDA. The planned 2026 capital programme of USD 1.35 billion to USD 1.45 billion is largely discretionary on held-by-production acreage, which gives Chord the lever to protect free cash flow if prices fall.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 110; calculation K6; calculation K9
### Porter's five forces

Rivalry and substitutes matter through price: Chord is a price taker in a commodity market, and energy-transition and supply decisions by other producers set the price that drives cash flow. Buyer power is concentrated but limited on price because realised prices follow NYMEX WTI and other purchasers exist, while supplier power shows in service-cost inflation and in a limited set of midstream providers; new entrants are unlikely to match the acreage position quickly, an Analyst Judgement that supports Chord's standing without changing price exposure.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40
### PEST analysis

Political and economic factors are the material categories. Geopolitical disruption raised oil prices in 2026, and a change in OPEC+ policy, including a member leaving the group in May 2026, could reverse them; tribal and federal regulation on the Fort Berthold Reservation and a title dispute with the MHA Nation add a regulatory and legal exposure whose size is not stated. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the materials supplied.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 179–180
### SWOT analysis

Strengths are liquidity, low reported leverage and operator control; weaknesses are price dependence, payout policy and concentration. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are Marcellus Shale proceeds used to retain cash and a longer hedge book; threats are a price fall toward the FY2025 level, a pipeline outage and a debt-funded acquisition.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21
### Financial profile and credit quality

On the nine dimensions the profile reads strong for scale, liquidity and ability to refinance, average for competitive advantage, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, free cash flow stability and financial policy, and weak for diversification. Margin and free cash flow stability are rated average rather than strong because FY2025 EBITDA was only 54.05% of the last-twelve-months level; liquidity is strong on USD 2,774.4 million; refinancing is strong on no maturity before 2030 though no rating or market price is supplied; financial policy is average with medium governance risk.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation K11
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the near-term outlook is supportive but price-contingent. Tailwinds are the higher oil price, improved Williston Basin takeaway, a hedge floor on 47.27% of fourth-quarter 2026 volumes and the Marcellus Shale proceeds; headwinds are cost inflation, a rate rise in the third quarter of 2026 that tightens financial conditions, geopolitical reversal and the open 2027 hedge book. Over three to five years the question is whether payout policy and acquisitions keep leverage near its present level, which neither company guidance nor a rating in the sources settles.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation H1; calculation H2
### Downside scenario

The realistic downside is a return of the crude price to the FY2025 average of USD 62.78 per Bbl, 18.61% below the last-twelve-months average of USD 77.13 per Bbl, while distributions continue. On last-twelve-months volumes that price would cut revenue and EBITDA by the same amount, leaving EBITDA at 72.74% of its reported level and net leverage at 0.30x, or 0.34x after the buybacks to 2026-11-04; free cash flow would fall to 79.08% of distributions, so distributions would run at 1.26x free cash flow, although the annualised base dividend alone would still be covered. The break comes in cash, not in debt service: cash would cover 5.35 years of that shortfall, buybacks of USD 529.0 million capacity could be stopped, capital spending could be cut, and no maturity falls due before 2030. This is an Analyst Judgement anchored to the reported FY2025 price; it omits hedge settlements and lower production taxes, so it overstates the near-term shortfall.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chrd_chrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chrd_chrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation P1; calculation P2; calculation P3; calculation P4; calculation P5; calculation P6; calculation P7; calculation P8
### Overall credit view

Overall, Chord presents a strong liquidity and refinancing position and an adequate business profile, supported by low reported leverage, USD 2,774.4 million of liquidity and operator control, but credit quality is constrained by price dependence, a payout policy that has run near free cash flow and an unsupplied legal framework. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: strong at the current price and contingent on hedges and spending cuts if prices fall. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the oil price and on whether distributions stay below free cash flow, since nothing matures before 2030. The primary downside path is a crude price fall that turns free cash flow below distributions and draws down cash. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, covenant figures, an agency view and 2027 guidance.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation P1; calculation P8
